standard_prerequisites: The Gysin homomorphism attached to a triple consisting of an invertible sheaf, a nonzero meromorphic section and its effective Cartier divisor of zeros, and the compatibility of Gysin pullback with proper pushforward
Proper pushforward of cycles preserves rational equivalence, so that a vanishing result on a proper cover descends
The general Gysin and first Chern class compatibility, and the vanishing of the cap product with the first Chern class of the structure sheaf
core_obligations: Unwind rational equivalence: the cycle is a locally finite sum of divisors of rational functions on integral closed subspaces of dimension k plus two

Form the coproduct of those subspaces with its induced Cartier divisor and use the compatibility of Gysin pullback with proper pushforward to reduce the statement to the sum of the divisors on the coproduct
Reduce to the case of an integral space carrying the divisor of a single rational function
If the divisor equals the whole space, identify the Gysin pullback as the cap with the first Chern class of the sheaf and conclude that it is rationally equivalent to zero
If the divisor is strictly smaller, identify the Gysin pullback with the cap of the class of the divisor by the first Chern class of the structure sheaf of the divisor, which is the zero map
proof_roadmap: Reduce a rationally trivial cycle to a locally finite sum of divisors on a coproduct and descend by proper pushforward
Reduce to an integral space and a single rational function
Split into the case where the divisor is everything and the case where it is proper, and use the two identifications with Chern class caps
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is that the Gysin homomorphism is well defined on rational equivalence classes at source lines 3732-3737, label lemma-gysin-factors, whose proof occupies source lines 3739-3760. The proof is short but not a citation: it unwinds rational equivalence into a locally finite sum of divisors on integral closed subspaces, builds the coproduct of those subspaces together with its induced Cartier divisor, and uses the compatibility of Gysin pullback with proper pushforward, together with the known descent of rational equivalence along a proper pushforward, to reduce to an integral space carrying the divisor of one rational function. The two remaining cases are then settled by two different identifications of the Gysin pullback with Chern class caps, one of which is the zero map. The counted statement records neither the coproduct reduction nor the case distinction.
